title: The woman of Endor (1 Samuel 28)
hookLine: desperate Saul consults a medium, who then insists on feeding him
tomorrow: How are the mighty fallen (2 Samuel 1:17–27)

lines: NO DREAM, NO URIM, NO PROPHET.
cards: Samuel is dead and buried. The Philistine army is camped across the valley, and when Saul sees it, his heart trembles greatly. He asks God what to do, and nothing comes.
No dream. No answer by the Urim, the priest's lots. No prophet.
So the king does the thing he himself had outlawed. Saul had driven the mediums and ghost-raisers out of the land. Now he tells his servants: find me a woman who can call up the dead.
There's one at Endor. Saul puts on other clothes, and goes by night.

teach.b: The woman is wary. You know what Saul did to people like me, she says; are you setting a trap? The disguised king swears by the Lord she won't be punished, and asks for Samuel.
When she sees what comes up, she screams, because now she knows who her visitor is.

teach.h: AN OLD MAN IN A ROBE.
teach.b: She describes an old man coming up, wrapped in a robe. Readers have argued over what really happened in that room, and the text doesn't settle it. What it gives is Samuel's message, and it is crushing.
The kingdom has been torn from you. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me.
Saul falls full length on the ground, no strength left; he hasn't eaten all day or all night. Here the story turns. The woman goes to him.
I took my life in my hand and listened to you, she says.
Now listen to me. Let me set a bit of bread before you, so you'll have strength for the road. He refuses.
His servants join in, and she keeps pressing, until he gets up off the floor and sits on the bed. She moves fast.

teach.h: THE CALF, THE BREAD, THE NIGHT.
teach.b: She kills the fatted calf in the house, kneads flour, bakes flat bread, and sets it before Saul and his servants. They eat, and go out into the night. The Torah forbids what she does for a living.
And the text still lets her be the one who shows Saul kindness that night.

how: Jews read Saul's night at Endor in the book of Samuel, part of the Prophets; the Torah forbids consulting mediums and the dead, and commentators have debated what happened in the woman's house.

o: a go-between who carries messages for a king
a prophet who answers the king by the Urim
one who claims to call up the spirits of the dead

games.q: the woman of Endor — tap the pairs.
p: one way God did not answer Saul
an old man in a robe
what the woman sees come up

s: Saul went to Endor in his royal robes
he disguised himself, put on other clothes, and went by night.
Saul had driven mediums out of the land himself
the chapter says so at its start, and the woman reminds him of it.
Saul ate the moment the woman offered food
he refused. his servants and the woman pressed him until he got up and ate.

games.q: you're the woman of Endor. the king who outlawed you is lying on your floor, with no strength, after hearing he'll die tomorrow. what do you do?
o: send him away before anyone finds out.
insist that he eat, and cook him a meal.
ask him to lift the ban on people like you.
games.why: she presses bread on him until he gives in, then kills her fatted calf and bakes bread for him and his servants.

practice: Let one person come to mind who's on the floor right now: grieving, exhausted, scared, out of options.

The woman of Endor didn't argue with Saul's fear or fix his future; she put bread in front of him, so think what the bread would be for your person, a meal at the door, coffee, sitting with them while they eat.
If you pray, you can hold their name.

wordCard.voice: medium. The woman at Endor the king had once outlawed, who saw Saul fall and wouldn't let him leave hungry. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a woman who calls up the dead, the medium Saul seeks in 1 Samuel 28:7.

carryVoice: Your line: she fed him. Looking back on the week: smooth stones, nefesh, window, the arrows, sparing Saul, Abigail, and the medium of Endor. Day seven hundred forty-two.
